title: Huldah's oracle: judgment on Jerusalem; Josiah gathered in peace (2 Kgs 22:15–20)
speaker: Huldah the prophetess (speaking for the LORD)
description: The LORD will bring all the evil written in the book on "this place" and its inhabitants because they forsook him; but because Josiah humbled himself, he will be gathered to his grave in peace and will not see the evil (2 Kgs 22:16–20; 2 Chr 34:24–28).
in_text_interpretation: Kings itself narrates the outcome: the LORD did not turn from his wrath (23:26–27); Josiah was killed at Megiddo (23:29) and Jerusalem fell later (25:8–10).

interpretations.label: Judgment fulfilled in the Babylonian conquest (597–587/586); delayed beyond Josiah's lifetime
interpretations.framework: Traditional Jewish and Christian; historical narrative
proponents: Josephus (Ant. 10.4.2: God "would at present delay those calamities" because Josiah was righteous)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Kings links the destruction to Manasseh's provocation and to this oracle (23:26–27; 24:3–4). Historical evidence: Jerusalem was taken in 597 (ABC 5) and the Temple burned in 587/586; Josiah died in 609, before any of this. Objection: the fulfilment is narrated by the same history that records the oracle; there is no independent witness to the oracle itself.

interpretations.label: "Gathered to your grave in peace" fulfilled in Josiah's death before the catastrophe, though he died in battle
proponents: C. F. Keil (1872): the phrase is used also of death in battle (1 Kgs 22:34, 40); "in peace" = without seeing the devastation
J. R. Lumby (1887): none of the threatened evils would come in his time
D. Guzik: three senses — before the disaster, at peace with God, in God's favour
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: 22:20 explains "in peace" by "your eyes will not see all the evil". Objection: Josiah was killed by Necho (23:29) — a tension readers have noticed; the harmonisation rests on the meaning of the formula, which Keil supports from 1 Kgs 22. A view that the oracle was composed before Josiah's death and not revised was not found in the sources read and is not attributed here.
